assumptions.obligation: i_a_valid is 0 while rst_ni = 0 and in the first cycle after reset release

TL-UL host rule: once i_a_valid=1 and o_a_ready=0, i_a_valid stays 1 and all A-channel fields (opcode, param, size, source, address, mask, data, instr, intg_flip) stay stable until the request is accepted
A new request never reuses the a_source of a request that is still outstanding (accepted but not yet answered on the D channel); tracking is cleared by reset
Requests at offset 0x400 and above are not issued (i_a_address[31:10] = 0 while i_a_valid)
No write request (PutFullData/PutPartialData) is issued with i_a_instr = 1
No combined ALERT_TEST write (offset 0x0C, bytes 0 and 3 written) that sets fatal_fault (bit 0) and clears regwen (bit 31) in one write, i.e. 0x0000_0001; tests use 0x8000_0001
When GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1: i_strap_en is 0 while rst_ni = 0 and for at least the first 4 cycles after reset release
When GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1: at the first rising edge of i_strap_en after reset, i_gpio has been constant for the 24 preceding cycles
When GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1: i_gpio stays constant for 8 cycles after the first rising edge of i_strap_en

After an accepted write that may change CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[i] (write to 0x3C with the byte lane of bit i enabled, or to PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i at 0x204+8*i with byte 0 enabled), i_gpio[i] is kept constant for 24 cycles

notes: Left unconstrained on purpose, because the spec treats these as legal inputs that get an error or must be handled: undefined opcodes, a_size=3, odd or misaligned masks and addresses, a_param values, i_a_intg_flip=1, instruction-fetch reads, i_d_ready back-pressure, toggling i_strap_en after the first strap sample, and i_gpio outside the windows above. GP-2-03/GP-2-04/GP-2-05 (when i_gpio may change, reset timing) need no assumption: with one clock the formal model already behaves that way. Offsets I inferred from the spec's register list (18 registers at 0x0-0x44, INTR_* at 0x0-0x8): ALERT_TEST=0x0C, CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER=0x3C, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i=0x204+8*i with filter enable at bit 4. ENV-10 is a little stronger than GP-10-09: the register value isn't visible from the interface, so any accepted write to these registers freezes the affected bits, not just writes that change the setting. The 24-cycle window starts when the write is accepted. ENV-06 forbids any full write that sets fatal_fault with regwen=0, not only the exact value 0x0000_0001. ENV-03 clears a source when its response arrives on o_d_source.
